title: ADDENDA: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY
text:
24        ADDENDA: A SUPPLEMENTAL HISTORY

AMARANTHINE

Did ever an artist, ancient or modern,
    Presume he could blot from the sky
The live, golden tints of an evening sunset?
    Most surely, he never would try.

The firm rock of ages can never be moved
    So long as the earth makes its round,
While deep in the hearts of all music lovers
    Will songs of Stephen Foster be found.

Years have passed swiftly, and removed from our ranks
    Of action, some men great of mind,
Yet, torches they lighted as they passed along,
    Leave a permanent path behind.

We speak of Halsell and Holland and Harshaw,
    And others who added their bit
To the wisdom of these outstanding teachers,
    Whose names in gold letters are writ.

Monuments left to the world at their passing,
    Were not cut from marble, or stone,
But chiseled from minds of brave lads and lassies,
    Through whom their reflection has shone.

The spark of ambition, early ignited
    By masters of wisdom and truth,
Has led ever on to a glad fruition,
    For many a strong-minded youth.

Then, none will presume that the ages of Time
    Can erase from sands on the shore,
The footprints Savoy College students have made—
    They're there, and will be, evermore.

—Martha Buford May.
notes: Page 24 of appendix. Poem 'Amaranthine' by Martha Buford May.
